topic: Authentication and launching: CSRF, authentication-ticket, hardware-backed auth (HBA/BAT), cookie rotation, the roblox-player URI, PlaceLauncher, user agent and rate limits. Verified 2026-10-24 against the live roblox.com JS bundles, the docsite OpenAPI, curl probes without a cookie, and 2023-2026 staff and community sources.

findings.claim: Without a cookie, POST auth.roblox.com/v1/authentication-ticket and POST /v1/logout and /v2/logout all return 401 before any CSRF check, and they send no x-csrf-token. With a valid cookie, authentication-ticket itself returns 403 with x-csrf-token, so a separate 'logout to get a CSRF token' call is unnecessary.
findings.detail: Curl on 2026-10-24, no Cookie header. POST https://auth.roblox.com/v1/authentication-ticket returned 401 with body {"errors":[{"code":9002,"subcode":0,"message":"Authentication token is missing"}]}. The response carried roblox-machine-id and x-envoy-*, so the route exists. GET on the same path returned 404 from ingress and a nonexistent path returned 404, which also shows the POST route is real. POST /v1/logout and /v2/logout returned the same 401 9002/0 and no x-csrf-token, so the old trick of getting a token from logout without a cookie no longer works. ic3w0lf22 Roblox-Account-Manager (RAM) Account.cs, GetCSRFToken: it POSTs v1/authentication-ticket/ with the cookie and Referer but no token, expects 403, and reads the x-csrf-token response header. GetAuthTicket then repeats the POST with X-CSRF-TOKEN. ethanstoner fork issue #8 (2026-09-23) confirms '401 before the CSRF check' happens only without a cookie. Risk with /v2/logout: if a cached valid token is attached, the session is destroyed. The website's own pattern is to send the real request, and on 403 with an x-csrf-token header, store the token and retry once.
sources: curl fixtures authlaunch-auth-ticket-nocookie-nocsrf.json, authlaunch-logout-v1-nocookie.json, authlaunch-logout-v2-nocookie.json, authlaunch-auth-ticket-get-nocookie.json, authlaunch-auth-nonexistent-path.json
findings.source_date: 2026-10-24 (curl); RAM code pre-2024-10 archive; fork issue 2026-09-23

findings.claim: The CSRF token is per session, not per subdomain. The website keeps one token for every *.roblox.com host, refreshes it only when a request returns 403 with an x-csrf-token header, and needs no TTL. The body of a CSRF failure differs by host, so detect it by the status code plus the header.
findings.detail: CoreUtilities.js has a class that stores the token in localStorage under key 'x-csrf-token' and adds it to every POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE. On 403 with an x-csrf-token header it stores the new token and retries, whatever the host. XsrfProtection.js seeds the token from <meta name='csrf-token' data-token>. Its 300 s staleness rule applies only to injected form posts, and its GET /XsrfToken refresh path now returns 404. Without a cookie, the token was identical (9BPntHEa3vgM) on auth.roblox.com POST /v2/login, on apis.roblox.com POST /sharelinks/v1/resolve-link, and in the page meta tag, from 10:47 to 11:05Z. Sending it back moved /v2/login past CSRF to a 400 error (code 3), so it was accepted. CSRF failure bodies: auth.roblox.com gives {"code":0,"message":"Token Validation Failed"} (flat), apis.roblox.com gives {"errors":[{"code":0,"message":"XSRF token invalid"}]}. Not every POST needs CSRF: users.roblox.com POST /v1/usernames/users returned 200 without a token. That the token is bound to the cookie session is inferred from the shared-store design and the long-standing behaviour seen in RAM.

findings.claim: The swagger docs are no longer served from the API subdomains. The published auth OpenAPI leaves out authentication-ticket and /redeem but documents the new GET /v1/client-assertion.
findings.detail: https://auth.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 and /v2 return 404 {"errors":[{"code":0,"message":""}]}. https://users.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 302-redirects to https://prod.docsiteassets.roblox.com/assets/en-us/cloud/legacy/users/v1.json. The auth spec lives at https://prod.docsiteassets.roblox.com/assets/en-us/cloud/legacy/auth/v1.json (also v2.json and v3.json; Last-Modified 2026-10-23). GET /v1/client-assertion has tag AuthenticationTicket, summary 'Creates a client assertion to be used when generating an auth ticket.', 200 schema GetClientAssertionResponse {clientAssertion: string}, and 401 when unauthenticated (confirmed by curl: 401 9002/0). Other documented endpoints: POST /v1/session/refresh and /v2/session/refresh ('Logs out user from the current session and create a new one'); POST /v2/logoutfromallsessionsandreauthenticate; POST /v3/logout with body {logoutReason, url, userId}. The SecureAuthenticationIntentModel {clientPublicKey, clientEpochTimestamp(int64), saiSignature, serverNonce} appears in the login, signup and password-change models. The gamejoin docsite JSON returns 403.

findings.claim: Today the website builds the auth ticket in two steps: GET https://auth.roblox.com/v1/client-assertion/, then POST https://auth.roblox.com/v1/authentication-ticket/ with a JSON body that is the assertion response, or {} if that GET failed. The ticket comes back in the rbx-authentication-ticket response header.
findings.detail: GameLaunch.js (served 2026-10-24) has two copies. The shared launcher function rb() does X.getUntyped(authApi+'/v1/client-assertion/',{credentials:'include'}), then X.fetch(authApi+'/v1/authentication-ticket/',{method:'POST',credentials:'include',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON(assertion ?? {})}), then headers.get('rbx-authentication-ticket'). The legacy function pZ() does the same with er.get and er.post. A ticket is requested only when the user is signed in and the launch mode is 'play'. It is requested right before the launch, never cached. RAM 3.7.x sends no body, and fork issue #8 (2026-09-23, P0, needs-account-test) flags the mismatch. Because the website itself falls back to {} when client-assertion fails, the server very likely still accepts an empty or {} body. That is inferred and has not been tested with a real account.

findings.claim: Headers for authentication-ticket: Cookie .ROBLOSECURITY, x-csrf-token, a roblox.com Referer, and Content-Type application/json. The browser also sends Origin https://www.roblox.com and, when HBA applies, x-bound-auth-token. The ticket is returned only in the rbx-authentication-ticket response header.
findings.detail: Referer: a 2022-03-13 DevForum thread shows a body with code 2 'The UrlReferrer was invalid or came from outside Roblox.' when the Referer was missing; the fix was 'Referer: https://www.roblox.com'. This may be stale. RAM sends Referer https://www.roblox.com/games/4924922222/Brookhaven-RP and no Origin. A CORS request with Origin https://www.roblox.com got access-control-allow-origin: https://www.roblox.com and access-control-allow-credentials: true. Whether Origin is strictly required is unknown. The trailing slash ('/v1/authentication-ticket/') is what both the website and RAM use; the path without it also exists. RBXAuthenticationNegotiation is only relevant to POST /v1/authentication-ticket/redeem, which the Roblox client calls, not RoALT. Without a cookie, redeem returned 403 {"errors":[{"code":4,"message":"Authentication ticket was invalid."}]} with or without that header.

findings.claim: HBA is live on roblox.com. Login registers a browser key (secure authentication intent) and the site signs API requests with x-bound-auth-token, including requests to auth.roblox.com and gamejoin.roblox.com.
findings.detail: The live tag <meta name='hardware-backed-authentication-data'> on www.roblox.com/games/1818 (2026-10-24, unauthenticated) has: data-is-secure-authentication-intent-enabled='true'; data-is-bound-auth-token-enabled='true'; data-bound-auth-token-whitelist={Whitelist:[49 entries, all sampleRate '100' except 'jQuery' at 1000000], including auth.roblox.com, gamejoin.roblox.com, games, users, friends, presence, thumbnails, economy, accountsettings, accountinformation, trades, billing, inventory, groups and others}; data-bound-auth-token-exemptlist={Exemptlist:[]}; data-hba-indexed-db-name='hbaDB'; data-hba-indexed-db-obj-store-name='hbaObjectStore'; data-hba-indexed-db-key-name='hba_keys'; data-hba-indexed-db-version='1'; data-bat-event-sample-rate='500'. Also <meta name='account-switching-data' data-is-account-switching-enabled='true'>. The roblox-bat README names the database 'hbaStore', but the live value is 'hbaDB', so read it from the meta tag rather than hard-coding it.

findings.claim: Exact HBA/BAT algorithm used by the website: an ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 key that is generated non-extractable and kept in IndexedDB, registered at login via secureAuthenticationIntent, and used to sign 'v1|bodyHash|ts|sig1|sig2'.
findings.detail: From CoreUtilities.js (modules Roblox.core-scripts.auth.boundAuth, hba, sai and crypto). Key: crypto.subtle.generateKey({name:'ECDSA',namedCurve:'P-256'}, false, ['sign']). Public key is base64 of the SPKI encoding. Signatures are base64 of WebCrypto raw r||s. SAI: the nonce is GET https://apis.roblox.com/hba-service/v1/getServerNonce, which returns a JSON string such as "QCD4CF44JQJDK4Y8", works unauthenticated and has an x-ratelimit of 50/60s. The SAI object is {clientPublicKey, clientEpochTimestamp: floor(now/1000), serverNonce, saiSignature: sign(`${pub}|${ts}|${nonce}`)}; it is skipped inside the Roblox app. BAT: bodyHash = base64(SHA-256(body string)), and an empty body gives 47DEQpj8HBSa+/TImW+5JCeuQeRkm5NMpJWZG3hSuFU=. ts = floor(now/1000). sig1 signs `${bodyHash}|${ts}|${fullUrl}|${METHOD}`; sig2 signs `|${ts}|${pathname}|${METHOD}`. Header: x-bound-auth-token: v1|bodyHash|ts|sig1|sig2. It is attached only when signed in, the host ends with .roblox.com, .robloxlabs.com or .roblox.qq.com, the flag is enabled and a key exists. Because the private key is non-extractable, a native client cannot export it from a browser or WebView2 profile.

findings.claim: I could not confirm whether the server enforces BAT. Community sources from 2026 say a plain HTTP client sending unsigned requests with a bound cookie (including authentication-ticket) still works. The website's own code identifies the failure as 401 with code 9002 and subcode 2. Sending a BAT signed with an unregistered key is rejected.
findings.detail: In CoreUtilities, predicate IK() checks status 401 && errors[0].code===9002 && errors[0].subcode===2, then calls onHbaUnauthorized, which dispatches the DOM event 'rbx:hba-unauthorized'. A missing cookie instead gives 9002 with subcode 0 'Authentication token is missing' (observed). ethanstoner fork issue #10 (2026-09-23) says 'enforcement for unsigned requests appears to be off now' and that cookies taken from a throwaway Chromium profile will stop launching if it is turned on; it gives no test evidence. The roblox-bat README (RoSeal; commits through 2026-10-09) says 'As of 2026, it is unknown when enforcement will begin again', which implies enforcement was active for a while earlier. The RoZod auth guide says 'a freshly generated pair produces tokens Roblox rejects', so keys must be the pair registered to that session. roblox-bat added SAI generation (2026-04-09), so a non-browser client can register its own key at login. Without credentials I could not test which endpoints, if any, enforce BAT today.

findings.claim: Roblox staff announced Account Session Protection, which binds a cookie to its device. It was to enforce the whole auth.roblox.com domain plus selected accountinformation, trades and billing endpoints, and accounts can opt out in Creator Hub under Settings -> Advanced.
findings.detail: DevForum post by jack_robloxman (Roblox Staff), created 2023-10-30. Enforcement moved from 2024-01-15 to 'by the end of June 2024 at the latest'. auth.roblox.com is enforced as a whole domain. accountinformation: GET/POST v1/birthdate, v1/gender, v1/phone, POST v1/phone/delete, /resend, /verify, POST/DELETE v1/star-code-affiliates, POST v1/email/verify. trades: accept, counter, decline, expire-outdated, send. billing: the whole domain. Friends, economy, users, inventory and groups were left for later. Open Cloud keys and OAuth2 tokens are unaffected. The post asks developers not to tell users to disable the protection. The 2026 roblox-bat README links to the opt-out help article, so the toggle probably still exists. The source is 2023-24 and may be stale; how this relates to HBA/BAT is inferred.

findings.claim: Roblox now rotates .ROBLOSECURITY. A new value can arrive in a Set-Cookie header on any normal API response, every few hours to days, and the app must overwrite its stored cookie. Breaking format changes apply on or after 2026-05-01.
findings.detail: Staff announcement 'Upcoming .ROBLOSECURITY Cookie Format Changes' (ttaahw, 2026-02-03). Roblox responds normally and adds 'Set-Cookie: .ROBLOSECURITY=<Cookie Value>; <attributes>' 'on a varying cadence of hours to days (and not on every request)'. 'you will always have a few months to process the header before Roblox begins to reject your outdated auth cookie'. Asked whether clients should overwrite the stored cookie, staff replied 'Exactly right!'. An invalid cookie gives 401. Outdated formats match ^(_\|WARNING:-DO-NOT-SHARE-THIS\.--Sharing-this-will-allow-someone-to-log-in-as-you-and-to-steal-your-ROBUX-and-items\.\|_)(GgIQAQ\.)?([0-9A-F]+)$. New cookies have used other formats 'for several months', and formats may change without notice, so the value must be treated as opaque. Neither the post nor the thread covers IP binding, HBA, or whether the old value stops working immediately; the grace window implies it does not. The fork's issue #11 says the old cookie-refresh endpoint www.roblox.com/authentication/signoutfromallsessionsandreauthenticate now returns 404 and points to auth.roblox.com/v2/logoutfromallsessionsandreauthenticate. That call signs out every other session, so it should not be used for routine refresh.

findings.claim: When the Roblox client redeems a ticket it gets its own session. The cookie RoALT stores is not changed by launching, but it can still rotate on any API response, as in A10.
findings.detail: The redeem endpoint POST https://auth.roblox.com/v1/authentication-ticket/redeem is live: an invalid ticket returns 403 code 4 'Authentication ticket was invalid.', rate-limited to 50 per 60 s. RAM and its fork have never re-read the cookie after a launch; RAM updates the stored cookie only after ChangePassword or LogOutOfOtherSessions. No source says redemption rotates or invalidates the issuing cookie. It is not known whether the ticket is single-use or how long it lives; the website fetches it immediately before launching.

findings.claim: Since 2022, cookies are reportedly tied to an IP region: using a cookie from a different region can reset the session. This matters for VPN changes, not for local use on the machine that logged in.
findings.detail: DevForum threads ('IP Changes Invalidate Cookie' 1700515; 'How to stop Roblox from resetting .ROBLOSECURITY during IP change' 2231529) report a rollout from 2022-03-08. When a request comes from a different region than the login, the token is reset; behaviour varies by region. In the 2026 cookie-format thread, community members say cookies are 'already partly IP-tied', with no staff confirmation. These reports are from users, not staff, and the 2022 material may be stale.

findings.claim: Exact roblox-player URI the website builds today: 'roblox-player:' followed by '+'-joined tokens in the order 1, launchmode:play, gameinfo:<encodeURIComponent(ticket)>, launchtime:<ms>, placelauncherurl:<encodeURIComponent(url)>, browsertrackerid:<id>, robloxLocale:en_us, gameLocale:en_us, [channel:<c>], LaunchExp:InApp.
findings.detail: From GameLaunch.js rP() and pZ() (protocolUrlSeparator '+'). n=['1','launchmode:'+mode]; gameinfo is added only when a ticket exists, as encodeURIComponent(ticket); launchtime=Date.now(). distributorType:Global, userId:<id> and browser:<name> are added only for studio modes (edit, plugin, asset). Other params are emitted as key:encodeURIComponent(String(v)), or as the bare key when key===value. Other params are inserted in this order: placelauncherurl (from the caller), then browsertrackerid, robloxLocale (data-protocol-roblox-locale), gameLocale, channel, LaunchExp. channel is omitted on Windows and Mac when data-is-omit-player-channel-for-win-and-mac-enabled='true', which is live today; in Aug 2025 the site sent an empty 'channel:' instead. LaunchExp is 'InApp' when data-is-duar-auto-opt-in-enabled and data-is-duar-opt-out-disabled are both true (both live), otherwise 'PreferInApp'. The URI is delivered by navigating a hidden <iframe id='gamelaunch'> to it. Live example: roblox-player:1+launchmode:play+gameinfo:<TICKET>+launchtime:1792839000000+placelauncherurl:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.roblox.com%2FGame%2FPlaceLauncher.ashx%3Frequest%3DRequestGame%26browserTrackerId%3D1234567890%26placeId%3D1818%26isPlayTogetherGame%3Dfalse%26joinAttemptId%3D<uuid>%26joinAttemptOrigin%3DPlayButton+browsertrackerid:1234567890+robloxLocale:en_us+gameLocale:en_us+LaunchExp:InApp. RAM sends an unencoded ticket and '+channel:+LaunchExp:InApp'. Bloxstrap matches channel with the regex 'channel:([a-zA-Z0-9-_]+)' and recognises both the 'roblox-player:' and 'roblox:' prefixes.

findings.claim: The PlaceLauncher base URL the website uses is https://www.roblox.com/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx, not assetgame. Both hosts now answer that path exactly as they answer a nonexistent path, so the URL appears to be only a parameter carrier the client parses (inferred).
findings.detail: GameLaunch.js pJ(): W.Endpoints.getAbsoluteUrl('/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx'). The Roblox.Endpoints.Urls map (ny in CoreUtilities) has no placelauncher entry, so it falls back to location.protocol + '//' + hostname + path, giving https://www.roblox.com/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx. Unauthenticated probes on 2026-10-24: https://assetgame.roblox.com/game/PlaceLauncher.ashx?... returns 301 to https://www.roblox.com/request-error?code=404, identical to assetgame /game/zzNonexistent.ashx. https://www.roblox.com/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx?... and /game/placelauncher.ashx return 404 with a 61,223-byte HTML page, byte-identical to /Game/zzNonexistent.ashx. /Game/Join.ashx also returns 404. I could not test an authenticated client request. RAM still builds https://assetgame.roblox.com/game/PlaceLauncher.ashx?...; the fork's issue list (Sep 2026) does not report launching as broken, which suggests the client parses the query whatever the host (inferred).

findings.claim: PlaceLauncher request types and parameters, as the website sends them now: RequestGame, RequestGameJob (gameId=jobId), RequestPrivateGame (accessCode and/or linkCode), RequestFollowUser (userId) and RequestPlayTogetherGame (conversationId). Every query starts with request=<type>&browserTrackerId=<id>.
findings.detail: Built in GameLaunch.js by c() / pQ(). Keys and values are encodeURIComponent'd, joined with '&', and '%20' becomes '+'; then the whole URL is encodeURIComponent'd again inside the URI. joinMultiplayerGame (RequestGame): placeId, launchData?, eventId?, isPlayTogetherGame=false, referredByPlayerId?, joinAttemptId (fresh UUID), joinAttemptOrigin (e.g. 'PlayButton'). joinGameInstance (RequestGameJob): placeId, gameId=<jobId>, isPlayTogetherGame, referredByPlayerId?, joinAttemptId, joinAttemptOrigin. joinPrivateGame (RequestPrivateGame): placeId, accessCode, linkCode, joinAttemptId, joinAttemptOrigin. Server-list joins pass accessCode with linkCode ''; share-link and privateServerLinkCode joins pass linkCode only (rG -> joinPrivateGame({placeId, linkCode})), so there is no need to scrape the access code from the game page as RAM does. followPlayerIntoGame (RequestFollowUser): userId, joinAttemptId, joinAttemptOrigin. playTogetherGame: placeId, conversationId. The shared launcher drops undefined params; the legacy jQuery.param path, active because data-is-www-common-game-launcher-enabled='false', emits them empty (launchData=&eventId=&referredByPlayerId=). Origin strings found: 'PlayButton', 'JoinInstance', 'JoinUser', 'ServerListJoin', 'privateServerJoin'. New /share?code=...&type=Server links resolve via POST https://apis.roblox.com/sharelinks/v1/resolve-link, which is CSRF-protected (unauthenticated: 403 'XSRF token invalid'); its body schema is unconfirmed.

findings.claim: No newer authenticated web launch path has replaced roblox-player plus placelauncherurl. roblox:// deep links carry no ticket and are marked deprecated. gamejoin.roblox.com is called by the client, not by the website, for player launches.
findings.detail: The website's only other player entry points are startDeepLinkFlow and startGameWithDeepLinkUrl (they open a URL as-is) and openDesktopUniversalApp (launchmode:app with LaunchExp:InApp and no place). create.roblox.com/docs/production/promotion/deeplinks (last_updated 2026-10-23) says 'This process is deprecated. To create public deep links, use share links.' It lists roblox://placeId=<id>&launchData=<string> and https://www.roblox.com/games/start?placeId=..., with parameters placeId, userId, launchData (≤200 bytes decoded), gameInstanceId, accessCode and linkCode, and says nothing about authentication. These links would run as whichever account the desktop app is already signed into, so they cannot launch a chosen account. Before launching, the website POSTs https://apis.roblox.com/matchmaking-api/v1/client-status with {"status":"Unknown"}; unauthenticated it returns 200 {"success":false}. It looks like a status beacon and appears optional. The only gamejoin call in GameLaunch.js is team-create-preemptive for Studio. Unauthenticated, gamejoin POST /v1/join-game returns 200 {status:12,message:'Unable to join Game 212'} and /v1/join-game-instance returns 401 9002/0, both limited to 5 per 1 s.

findings.claim: Launch-process facts relevant to multi-instance: Bloxstrap passes the raw URI as RobloxPlayerBeta's only argument. Clients started from a URI have no -t or -j flags. Roblox now autostarts a tray process that holds the singleton handles. Bloxstrap dropped multi-instance in v2.10.0.
findings.detail: Bloxstrap Bootstrapper.StartRoblox sets ProcessStartInfo{FileName=RobloxPlayerBeta path, Arguments=_launchCommandLine (the URI), WorkingDirectory=version dir}; the URI has been passed directly since Bloxstrap v2.6.0 (March 2024, per the wiki deep-dive). LaunchHandler checks Mutex 'ROBLOX_singletonMutex'. Fork issue #7 (2026-09-23) says clients also check 'ROBLOX_singletonEvent', and that 'RobloxPlayerBeta.exe --launch-to-tray' is started from the Windows Run key and takes both handles; client 0.740. Fork issue #13 says URI-launched clients lack -t/-j, so process watchers must track PIDs at launch. Bloxstrap v2.10.0 (2025-10-01) removed multi-instance because 'Roblox broke it'.

findings.claim: No User-Agent is required at the unauthenticated stage of authentication-ticket. auth.roblox.com sits behind Cloudflare Bot Management; the other API hosts are behind 'public-gateway'.
findings.detail: POST /v1/authentication-ticket gave the identical 401 9002/0 with a Chrome 141 UA, curl's default UA, an empty UA and 'Roblox/WinInet'. auth.roblox.com responses carry server: cloudflare, cf-cache-status and Set-Cookie __cf_bm (Domain=roblox.com, 30-minute expiry), which marks Cloudflare Bot Management. gamejoin, apis and www answer with server: public-gateway and set rbx-ip2, GuestData and RBXEventTrackerV2. Whether Cloudflare challenges authenticated traffic from non-browser clients is unknown. RAM sets no UA in Account.cs and leaves it to RestSharp's default.

findings.claim: Rate limits are advertised per route in RateLimit-style headers ('x-ratelimit-limit: N, N;w=SECONDS', x-ratelimit-remaining, x-ratelimit-reset). The authenticated limit for authentication-ticket is unknown.
findings.detail: Observed without a cookie, per IP: auth/v1/authentication-ticket (401 path) 1000/60s; auth/v1/authentication-ticket/redeem 50/60s; auth/v2/login 750/3600s; auth/v1/logout and /v2/logout 1000/60s; auth/v1/client-assertion 1000/60s; apis/hba-service/v1/getServerNonce 50/60s; gamejoin/v1/join-game and join-game-instance '5, 5;w=1', plus minimum-retry-wait-seconds: 1; users/v1/usernames/users 500/60s; apis/matchmaking-api/v1/client-status 100/60s; assetgame 404 redirect 100/60s. The remaining count on authentication-ticket fell 999→998→997 across calls with different UAs, so the bucket is per IP and per route when unauthenticated. The RAM README says that failures when repeatedly launching multiple accounts come from rate limiting, but gives no figures.

findings.claim: Any Roblox API call can return a generic challenge: 403 with rblx-challenge-id, rblx-challenge-type and rblx-challenge-metadata headers. The website renders the challenge and retries the request.
findings.detail: The CoreUtilities HTTP interceptor reads 'rblx-challenge-id', 'rblx-challenge-type' and 'rblx-challenge-metadata' (base64 JSON), renders the challenge in 'generic-challenge-container', and retries the request. Challenge bundles on the page include CaptchaV2Challenge, ProofOfWorkChallenge, ProofOfSpaceChallenge, PrivateAccessTokenChallenge, DeviceIntegrityChallenge, Reauthentication, TwoStepVerification and Rostile. RoZod exposes {challengeType, challengeId, challengeBase64Metadata} and retries up to 3 times. Whether authentication-ticket itself triggers challenges is unknown.

findings.claim: browserTrackerId comes from the RBXEventTrackerV2 cookie that www.roblox.com sets, holding a 16-digit browserid. Launch IDs must be validated because '+' and '&' inside values inject extra parameters.
findings.detail: Set-Cookie: RBXEventTrackerV2=<redacted>; domain=roblox.com; expires 2054. GameLaunch pi() reads it with /browserid=([^&]*)/. RAM instead makes a random number per account by concatenating two random ints of 6 digits each. pealz1/RobloxAccountManager issue #1 (2026-10-03) shows that a jobId of 'abc+placelauncherurl:https://example.com/x' or a placeId of '123&isPlayTogetherGame=true' alters the launch. That issue proposes ASCII-only regexes. Note: accessCode and jobId are UUIDs with dashes, and private-server link codes are digit strings (my observation, not stated in the issue).

open_questions: Does POST /v1/authentication-ticket/ still accept an empty or {} body, or is the clientAssertion from GET /v1/client-assertion/ now required? This needs one test with a real account. The website falls back to {} when the assertion GET fails, which suggests the empty body is still accepted.

Does any endpoint currently enforce x-bound-auth-token (BAT) for sessions created with secure authentication intent? If so, is authentication-ticket one of them, and what is the exact 401 body? The web code uses code 9002 with subcode 2.
What is the authenticated, per-user or per-cookie rate limit on authentication-ticket, and does a 429 include Retry-After?
How long does an authentication ticket live, and is it single-use?
With LaunchExp:InApp (the desktop app experience), does launching account B with a ticket replace the app's persisted login? Does it affect instances already running under account A?
Is PlaceLauncher.ashx truly gone server-side for authenticated client requests? Does the 0.74x client still accept an assetgame.roblox.com placelauncherurl, as RAM still sends?
What are the exact Set-Cookie attributes and structure of the new .ROBLOSECURITY formats? Does a session/refresh call or a rotation keep the HBA binding of the original session?
Is the Account Session Protection opt-out (Creator Hub > Settings > Advanced) still present in 2026, and how does it relate to HBA/BAT?
What request body does POST apis.roblox.com/sharelinks/v1/resolve-link expect for /share?code=...&type=Server links, and what does it return?
Does Cloudflare Bot Management on auth.roblox.com challenge authenticated non-browser clients, depending on UA or TLS fingerprint?
Is the Referer requirement on authentication-ticket (code 2 'UrlReferrer was invalid', 2022) still enforced, and is Origin also checked?
design_implications: auth: get the CSRF token from the request itself, not from a logout call. Send the real POST (authentication-ticket or any other) with the cached token. If the response is 403 and has an x-csrf-token header, store that token and retry once. Never use /v2/logout to prime the token: a cached valid token sent there destroys the session. Keep one token per account, valid for every *.roblox.com host, with no TTL; detect a CSRF failure from the status code plus the header, not from the body.

auth: get_ticket() should mirror the website. First GET https://auth.roblox.com/v1/client-assertion/ and ignore any failure. Then POST https://auth.roblox.com/v1/authentication-ticket/ with Content-Type application/json, body = the assertion JSON or {}, plus Cookie, x-csrf-token, Referer https://www.roblox.com/ and Origin https://www.roblox.com. Read the rbx-authentication-ticket header. Fetch the ticket immediately before each launch and never cache it.

auth: after every response from any roblox.com host, check Set-Cookie for '.ROBLOSECURITY=' and atomically persist the new value to the encrypted store before returning. Treat the cookie as an opaque string: no format regex and no length cap. Periodically 'touch' idle accounts with a cheap authenticated GET such as users.roblox.com/v1/users/authenticated so they pick up rotations before old formats are rejected (grace period: months).

auth: classify errors into types the UI can act on. 401 with code 9002 subcode 0, or other 401s: cookie dead, re-login needed. 401 with code 9002 subcode 2: HBA binding required. 403 with rblx-challenge-id/-type/-metadata: a challenge needs a human in the browser; never try to solve it. 403 with x-csrf-token: retry once. 429, or x-ratelimit-remaining at 0: back off until x-ratelimit-reset or Retry-After. Parse the 'N, N;w=S' header format generically.

auth/HBA: never send an x-bound-auth-token unless you hold the private key registered to that exact session; a wrong key is rejected, which is worse than sending none. Today, send unsigned requests from Rust and detect 9002/2. Keep one persistent WebView2 user-data folder per account from 'add account' onward; do not use a throwaway profile as RAM does. That keeps the browser's non-extractable HBA key alive, so if enforcement starts you can fall back to running the website's own ticket flow inside that profile, where Roblox's JS signs the request. A later option is to generate a Rust P-256 key and register it through secureAuthenticationIntent at login (format in fixture authlaunch-hba-bat-spec.json). That should be a deliberate later decision, not part of v1.

auth: read HBA settings from the live <meta name='hardware-backed-authentication-data'> tag (IndexedDB names, enabled flags) instead of hard-coding them; it already differs from the roblox-bat README ('hbaDB' vs 'hbaStore').

launcher: build the URI exactly as GameLaunch.js does. Use 'roblox-player:' + ['1','launchmode:play','gameinfo:'+enc(ticket),'launchtime:'+now_ms,'placelauncherurl:'+enc(plUrl),'browsertrackerid:'+btid,'robloxLocale:en_us','gameLocale:en_us','LaunchExp:InApp'].join('+'). enc = JS encodeURIComponent, i.e. a percent-encoding set that leaves A-Za-z0-9 and -_.!~*'() unescaped. Omit channel on Windows, as the site does. plUrl = https://www.roblox.com/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx?request=<T>&browserTrackerId=<id>&... with each key and value encoded and %20 replaced by '+'. Add joinAttemptId (UUIDv4) and joinAttemptOrigin=PlayButton. One unit test should compare the output byte for byte with the examples in authlaunch-web-launch-uri-spec.json.

launcher: support RequestGame(placeId), RequestGameJob(placeId, gameId=jobId), RequestPrivateGame(placeId, linkCode and/or accessCode) and RequestFollowUser(userId). Pass linkCode straight through; do not scrape the access code from the game page. Validate inputs before building: placeId and userId as ASCII digits that parse as u64; jobId and accessCode as UUIDs matching ^[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}$; linkCode as ^[0-9]+$. Reject anything else, so '+' and '&' injection is impossible even before encoding.

launcher: do not call PlaceLauncher.ashx or the gamejoin API yourself; the client does that from the URI. Do not use roblox:// deep links for per-account launches, because they carry no ticket and run as whoever the desktop app is signed into. Skip the matchmaking-api client-status beacon (YAGNI).

launcher: to track instances, start RobloxPlayerBeta.exe (or the handler registered under HKCR\roblox-player\shell\open\command, which may be Bloxstrap or Fishstrap) with the URI as a single argument, and record the PID and log path at spawn time. URI-launched clients have no -t or -j flags to match on later. Expect the '--launch-to-tray' autostart process to be holding ROBLOX_singletonMutex and ROBLOX_singletonEvent; multi-instance is a separate concern for the launcher.

launcher (bulk): launch strictly one at a time. For each account, fetch its ticket immediately before launching it, wait for the process to spawn (and for any singleton handling) before the next, add spacing with jitter, and honour x-ratelimit-* headers and 429s per IP. Keep a stable browserTrackerId per account: either the RBXEventTrackerV2 browserid captured from that account's WebView2 profile, or a random 16-digit number stored once.

http: use one reqwest Client and set the Cookie header per request, rather than one shared cookie jar for all accounts, so sessions cannot leak between accounts. Send a fixed, realistic browser User-Agent. Treat Cloudflare 403/503 HTML responses on auth.roblox.com as a separate 'blocked' error type from Roblox's JSON errors.
